channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: Opinion | In A Climate Of Cuts And Broken Trust, Nonprofits (119K To Zero Collective) Stand Firm For Our Young People
item.description: Leaders from five different nonprofits within the 119K To Zero Collective say recent news regarding the state audit of misappropriated funds in Hartford, combined with a harsh federal funding climate, have created a "perfect storm" for Connecticut’s nonprofit sector. Trust is being tested exactly when our services are most needed.

item.title: Blumenthal Bill Targets Gun Industry Advertising
item.description: The proposal, dubbed the Responsible Firearms Marketing Act would direct the Federal Trade Commission to launch an investigation into the advertising and marketing practices of gun manufacturers.

item.title: Agreement Reached In Free Speech Lawsuit
item.description: The ACLU Foundation of Connecticut and the Connecticut State Police have reached an agreement in a federal lawsuit over residents’ right to protest on highway overpasses.

item.title: Opinion | Ensuring Connecticut’s Taxes On Hospitals Support Patients
item.description: Connecticut Hospital Association CEO Jennifer Jackson says the governor's budget proposal puts Connecticut at a crossroads, because it will perpetuate the cycle of high taxes on and under-investment in care provided by hospitals, hurting patients, families, and the communities that depend on local care.

item.title: UI Customers Could See 11 Percent Drop In Rates
item.description: Connecticut customers may see an estimated 11 percent drop in their monthly electric bill starting in May, United Illuminating said in its new rate request.

item.title: CT Captive Audience Law Survives Legal Challenge From Business Lobby
item.description: Captive audience meetings are mandatory meetings held during work hours to pressure employees to support certain religious or political points of view, political candidates or to vote against forming a union.

item.title: Legislators Honor CT’s Future Business Leaders At Capitol
item.description: The celebration, hosted by state Rep. Kate Farrar, D-West Hartford, honored the roughly 2,000 FBLA members across 60 school districts.

item.title: Aid-In-Dying Advocates Once Again Face Uphill Fight In CT
item.description: Tim Appleton, Connecticut campaign director for the Compassion & Choices Action Network, said legislation legalizing aid in dying has been introduced in Connecticut 20 times since 1994 and had 10 public hearings over the years.

item.title: Religious, Education Groups Request Changes To Antisemitism Language In Education Bill That Passed CT House Last Year
item.description: H.B. 7009 was a broad education bill that among other things covered Islamic and Arabic studies, electronic devices in schools, kindergarten waivers and more. It passed the House in a bipartisan 128-20 vote but did not receive a vote in the Senate.

item.title: CT Police, Firefighters Could Get College Tuition, Mortgage Assistance Under Proposed Bill
item.description: On Tuesday, Gov. Ned Lamont announced House Bill 5046, An Act Supporting Firefighter and Police Officer Recruitment and Retention. The bill waives tuition and fees for police officers and firefighters with five or more years or service at all Connecticut public colleges and universities and also creates a mortgage assistance program to help the responders purchase a home in the communities where they serve.
